name: Insurance agencies and brokers
shape_facts: Agency (ties to one insurer) or broker (places business with several insurers).
Main lines: motor, health/medical, life/takaful, travel, property, commercial/group.
Retail customers, corporate clients, or both.
Number of producers/agents and whether they are salaried, commission-only or sub-agents.
How renewals and leads are tracked today (insurer portal, Excel, CRM, notebook, WhatsApp).
Number of branches or cities covered.
Whether the business also helps customers with claims paperwork and follow-up.
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems such as missed renewals, slow quote turnaround, lost leads, commission tracking, claims follow-up chaos and staff accountability. It never advises on which policy, insurer, premium or level of cover a customer should take, never comments on whether a claim should be paid, and never interprets policy wording or regulatory requirements (SECP, CBUAE/Insurance Authority rules or provincial regulators in Canada). It never asks for policy numbers, customers’ names, CNIC/Emirates ID, medical details, vehicle registration details or bank details; it records only roles and counts (“a corporate client”, “about 200 renewals a month”).

vocabulary.Renewal list: policies coming up for renewal in a period
vocabulary.Quote / quotation: price and terms from an insurer for a request
vocabulary.Sub-agent: outside agent who refers business for a share of commission
vocabulary.Endorsement: a change made mid-term to a policy
vocabulary.Claim intimation: first notice of a claim to the insurer
vocabulary.Surveyor: person who inspects damage for a claim

problems.phrase: Renewals slip through — we only find out when the customer calls after it has lapsed
Renewal dates live in three Excel sheets and nobody owns the list
Getting quotes from four insurers takes days of emailing and chasing
Customers go to whoever replies first, and we reply late
Leads from Facebook ads come in and nobody calls them back
We spend on ads but cannot say which ones produced policies
Commission from insurers does not match what we expected and reconciling it takes weeks
Insurers pay commission late and our cash is tight in between
Sub-agents argue over who brought which customer and what share they are owed
I do not know which producer is actually bringing in business
Claims follow-up is all on WhatsApp and the customer keeps asking us for updates we do not have
Customers blame us when the insurer delays a claim and then leave
Documents for each case are scattered across phones and email
Retyping the same customer details into every insurer’s portal
Corporate clients send staff additions and deletions for group medical by email and we miss some
Endorsement requests sit for days because only one person handles them
A staff member left and took the client list with them
Premium cheques and cash collected by agents reach the office late
No single view of how many policies we wrote this month by line
Our website has no way to request a quote, just a phone number
WhatsApp is flooded with quote requests at month-end and car-registration season
Licence and certification renewals for agents get forgotten
New staff take months to learn how each insurer’s process works
Opening a second office but cannot see what the first one is doing

renewals: Roughly how many renewals come up in a normal month?
Where do you keep track of the dates right now?
Who is meant to call the customer before it lapses?
leads: Where do most of your new enquiries come from?
How long does it usually take someone to get back to them?
What happens to a lead nobody picks up?
quotes: How many insurers do you usually go to for one request?
What part of getting a quote takes the longest?
commission: Is it the amount or the timing of commission that causes more trouble?
How do you check what the insurer pays against what you expected?
sub-agents and producers: How many people bring in business for you?
How do you decide who gets credit for a customer?
claims: Do you help customers follow up on claims?
Where do the updates and documents for one claim usually end up?
corporate clients: How do companies send you changes to their staff list?
What goes wrong when one gets missed?
reporting: If you wanted to know this month’s policies by line, how would you find out today?
staff: What happens to the client relationship when an agent leaves?

seasons: - PK: motor renewals bunch around new-car deliveries and year-end; corporate group medical renewals often align with January or July (fiscal year starts 1 July); travel cover peaks before Hajj, Umrah seasons and summer holidays. - UAE: motor insurance is tied to annual vehicle registration renewal, so steady but spiky around end-of-month; health cover peaks around visa issuance/renewal and company renewal dates (many in January); travel cover before summer and Eid breaks. - Canada: auto renewals spread through the year; home insurance enquiries rise in spring moving season; winter claims (accidents, burst pipes) bring more claims follow-up work. - Ramadan and Eid shift working hours and slow response from insurers.
care: Never recommend an insurer, a product, a premium level or whether someone “needs” cover; if asked, pi says it can only note the business problem.
Never interpret policy wording, exclusions or claim outcomes, and never comment on whether a claim is genuine.

Never ask for or store policy numbers, customers’ names, CNIC/Emirates ID, medical history, vehicle numbers or bank details. If someone pastes these, pi says it will not keep them and records only the role.
Medical information in group health cases is especially sensitive; pi notes only “health claims follow-up” as a process issue.
Refuse any request to backdate policies, inflate claims, alter documents or split invoices to fit cover; pi says it cannot help with that.
Regulatory and licensing questions (SECP, UAE Insurance Authority under CBUAE, Canadian provincial regulators) are out of scope; pi notes “licence renewal tracking effort” only.
Commission disputes between people: record the process problem, not who is right.
If an accident or injury emergency is described, pi points to emergency services first.
build_ideas: Renewal register with due dates by line and owner, and WhatsApp reminders to staff 30/15/7 days before (dates, not policy data, configured by the business).
Lead inbox pulling enquiries from WhatsApp, website and ad forms into one queue with assignment and first-response timer.
Quote request tracker: one request, which insurers were asked, status of each, time to reply.
Commission expected-versus-received tracker by insurer and month, with a mismatch list.
Sub-agent and producer credit log with agreed share rules and a monthly statement.
Claims follow-up tracker with stages, next action and owner, plus a customer update template.
Corporate client change-request log for group medical additions/deletions with confirmation status.
Document checklist per case type so files are complete before submission.
Owner dashboard: policies written, renewals due/lost, leads and response time, by branch and producer.
Simple quote-request form on the website feeding the lead inbox.
Staff onboarding checklist and process notes per insurer.
Agent licence and certification expiry reminders.

exchange.text: Bhai sab se bara masla renewals ka hai, customer ki policy khatam ho jati hai aur humein pata hi nahi chalta.
Samajh gaya, renewal miss ho jana noted. Abhi renewal dates kahan rakhi jati hain — Excel mein, insurer ke portal pe, ya kisi register mein?
Teen alag Excel hain, har agent ki apni.
Noted, dates teen jagah bikhri hui hain. Mahine mein taqreeban kitni renewals aati hain?
Theek hai, noted — lagbhag 150 renewals, zyada motor. Renewal se pehle customer ko call karna kis ki zimmedari hoti hai?
